candidates.name: Alcazaba
candidates.content: A Moorish castle built in the 11th century on a hill in the middle of the city, this old fort is the best-preserved of its kind in Spain. Upon entering you'll climb up past the ramparts offering excellent views of the city and lus

candidates.name: Picasso Museum
candidates.hours: Jul-Aug: daily 10:00-20:00; Mar-Jun Sep-Oct: daily 10:00-19:00; Nov-Dec: daily 10:00-18:00
candidates.content: The Picasso museum hosts exclusive paintings and other artworks by the Málaga-born artist. Your entry fee also provides access to regularly changing exhibitions by other artists.

candidates.name: Málaga Glass & Crystal Museum
candidates.alt: Museo del Vidrio y Crystal de Málaga
candidates.content: The museum has around 700 pieces of glass, dating from Phoenician times to the 20th century. Housed in a housed in an 18th-century casa palacio which is as fascinating as the objects within. Guided tours only, available in English

candidates.name: Malaga Aviation Museum
candidates.content: Unique museum with original 1940s terminal in Malaga, other buildings with old and new aviation equipment, uniforms, and models of the airport. Interesting for both children and adults. Free parking.

candidates.name: Málaga Cathedral
candidates.content: In the heart of the city centre and well worth visiting.

candidates.name: Russian Museum Collection, St. Petersburg-Málaga
candidates.content: It was the first European subsidiary of the Russian State Museum of Saint Petersburg. However, the museum's collection returned to Russia in May 2022 after concluding the last exhibition. Since then, the Malaga City Council has ke

candidates.name: Roman Theater
candidates.content: The beautiful remains of an old Roman theater. You can view them anytime from the overlook in the plaza, but if you want to get up close you can enter the attached building, where you'll be shown a short film and view some artifac

candidates.name: Museum Jorge Rando
candidates.hours: Mon-Fri 10:00-14:00 & 16:00-20:00 Sat 10:00-14:00 (Afternoon session is one hour later June-September)
candidates.content: Museum focussed on expressionist art.

candidates.name: Castillo de Gibralfaro
candidates.price: €3.50; reduced €1.50, free Sundays after 14:00. Combined ticket with Alcazaba €5.50
candidates.content: Another Moorish castle and the counterpart to the Alcazaba, the Castillo sits on a larger hill behind the Alcazaba and offers an incredible view of the city and neighboring suburbs from the ramparts that encircle the castillo. Wit

candidates.name: Centre Pompidou Málaga
candidates.content: Works from the Paris Centre Pompidou's collection.

candidates.name: Interactive Museum of Music
candidates.alt: Museo Interactivo de la Musica Málaga
candidates.content: Has one of the largest collections of musical instruments in Europe.

candidates.name: Automobile & Fashion Museum
candidates.alt: Museo del Automovil y la Moda
candidates.price: Adult €10; 65+ €8; other concessions & groups €6. (occasional dramatised openings at higher price, check website)
candidates.content: An interest combined museum showing vehicles & fashion through various eras. Located in a former tobacco factory.

candidates.name: MUCAC - La Coracha
candidates.content: Contemporary art museum that will be open on two sites.

candidates.name: Picasso's birthplace
candidates.content: Loads of objects and some paintings that the most famous artist of the 20th century created during his childhood.

candidates.name: Museo Carmen Thyssen
candidates.hours: Tue-Thu 10:00-20:00, Fri Sat 10:00-21:00, Sun and holidays 10:00-20:00 (open Mon and closed Sun in summer)
candidates.content: Opened in 2011 and has an excellent collection of 19th and 20th century Spanish paintings.

candidates.name: La Conception Botanical & Historical Garden
candidates.hours: Apr-Sep: Tue-Sun 09:30-20:30; Oct-Mar: Tue-Sun 09:30-17:30; closed Dec 25, Jan 1
candidates.content: Botanical and historical garden with beautiful views of the city from this garden; worth a visit.

candidates.name: MUCAC - Mayoristas
candidates.content: Former Centro de Arte Contemporáneo will reopen after refurbishment.

candidates.name: Plaza de Toros de la Malagueta
candidates.hours: Mon-Fri 10:00-13:00 and 17:00-20:00, closed Sat Sun and holidays
candidates.content: Málaga's bullring.

candidates.name: La Térmica
candidates.content: Former charity house of mercy. Now a cultural centre that hosts occasional exhibitions & small concerts.

candidates.name: Semana Santa
candidates.content: The Holy Week processions in Málaga are known for at least 500 years, and are one of the oldest in all of Spain. They begin Palm Sunday and end Easter Sunday. The Spanish Legion's procession is a must see on Maundy Thursday.

candidates.name: Sightseeing Treasure Hunt Málaga
candidates.hours: By appointment, tours last at least 2.5 hours
candidates.content: Malaga City Adventure is a startup company and pioneers in Treasure Hunting Events in Málaga. They offer a Sightseeing Treasure Hunt for tourists and tailor made team building events for companies. Equipped with a treasure hunting

candidates.name: La Trinchera
candidates.content: Concert Hall 2 km west of city centre.

candidates.name: Escapada Cycling
candidates.content: Gravel, e-bike, trekking and mountain bike rental, as well as guided cycling experiences.

candidates.name: La Cochera Caberet
candidates.content: Small music & theatre venue a couple of km out of the centre.

candidates.name: Central Beers
candidates.content: Good choice of Belgian beers. Busy at weekends.

candidates.name: Birras Deluxe
candidates.content: Belgian & American-style beers on tap with friendly staff. Food available.

candidates.name: Tako bar
candidates.content: Mainly Belgian beers with range of Tex-Mex food available.

candidates.name: Vegetariano El Calafate
candidates.content: A hidden gem around the corner from Thyssen Museum. Offers traditional Spanish & Andalucian dishes, with a vegetarian twist. Low-key interior with art for sale on the walls. Good choice for lunch and dinner.

candidates.name: Bodega-Bar El Pimpi
candidates.content: Enormously popular with locals and tourists, this place serves up excellent food and wine. Despite being frequented by such celebrities as Antonio Banderas and Placido Domingo, the prices are very moderate.

candidates.name: Restaurante Gallego Candamil
candidates.content: This Galician restaurant is very popular with the locals. This is understandable when you see the great range of quality tapas at fantastic prices, e.g. tapa of empanada €1.25, glass of cider €1.15.

candidates.name: Bodeguita El Gallo
candidates.content: Typical Andalusian tavern evironment, Sweet Málaga wines and the most traditional tapas.

candidates.name: Taberna Quitapenas Sánchez Pastor
candidates.content: Good place to go for tapas, nice atmosphere, good service. Authentic and friendly. Great wines.

candidates.name: Tasca La Salita
candidates.content: Yummy tapas (especially the pork) at a good price. Not a touristy place with tons of seats so get there early.

candidates.name: La Vegana
candidates.content: 100% vegan tapas bar. Saturday is Paella day. See website for hours & reservations.

candidates.name: Mesón Lo Güeno
candidates.content: Offers a large range of tapas and excellent wines.

candidates.name: Curry-Ya! Málaga
candidates.content: A very cozy establishment. As the name suggests, a wide variety of curry dishes. Ideal to spend some time with your close ones between spicy and sweet dishes with a Japanese essence. Good service and very good atmosphere.

candidates.name: Restaurante @ Parador de Málaga Gibralfaro
candidates.content: Castillo de Gibralfaro. Some report being disappointed by the restaurant at the Parador. The food was sub par, but the service by contrast was exemplary, together with all the nice little free appetizers, aperitifs, etc. Wine list

candidates.name: Taperia El Beato
candidates.content: Great terrace and fantastic service. Fresh fish, homemade croquettes, meatballs in delicious almond sauce.

candidates.name: La Campana
candidates.content: Cozy and typical Andalusian place of Malaga with a lot of history. Cozy atmosphere.

candidates.name: Central Market
candidates.content: A lively market featuring regional produce and olive oil, fish, meat, and cheese, housed in a 19th-century wrought iron building. Don't miss the restored, enormous stained glass windows, as well as the large 14th-century Moorish g

december.text: Málaga is a city of 590,000 people (2024) in the southern Spanish region of Andalucia, and the largest city on the Costa del Sol. The city offers beaches, hiking, architectural sites, art museums, and excellent shopping and cuisine. While more laid back than Madrid or Barcelona, Málaga is still the centre and transport

Renfe also operates two Cercanías commuter rail lines out of Málaga, one west along the coast via the airport C-1 and the nearby tourist towns of Torremolinos and Fuengirola and one inland C-2. The most typical thing to eat in Málaga is espetos, sardines squewered on a bamboo stick and grilled over a fire (typically driftwood); and pescaíto frito: all types of deep-fried fish from anchovies to squid. A speciality of Andalucia is fish (most commonly dogfish "cazon", although sometimes other fish such as tuna,

Cafetería of Hotel Castilla Guerrero, in street Córdoba, nº 7 in Málaga centre, between the Port and Alameda Principal. Offers traditional and typical Andalucian dishes, including soups, salads, meats and fishes or sandwiches, cakes, croissants or baguettes. Star dishes include: Gazpacho andaluz, Paella, Porra Antequer

Málaga has exceptional road and motorway links, making it an excellent base for exploring the nearby villages and towns. Wonderful drives inland reveal the hidden gems of this region, with small restaurants nestling in the hills where you can experience an authentic taste of Andalucia.
